predicts: continuous minimum temperature (deg C) over the configured horizon
training_description: India Tier 3: pooled 15 GSOD stations (Indo-Gangetic plains + central), Nov-Mar 1990-2024, core features (temperature + humidity only), next-day Tmin regression, CatBoost default parameters, refit on ALL seasons (48,811 station-days). Reported metrics are from the train-only model on the 2018-2024 test seasons at the validation-tuned threshold.
known_limitations: Trained and evaluated on Tier-1 European data (Basel, Oslo, Perpignan, De Bilt), NOT Indian data -- see the project's India-bridge notes before treating this as deployment-ready for Warora/Vidarbha.
Not yet benchmarked for latency/memory on the actual target hardware (Raspberry Pi) -- deferred per the project brief until hardware is available.
Hyperparameters were chosen via a modest, non-exhaustive search (see 05_model_training.ipynb); tuning did not clearly outperform CatBoost's own defaults in that search.
Labels are RULE-DERIVED (next-day Tmin <= 4 C), not observed frost or crop damage; skill is skill at the rule's conditions.
Pooled across stations; NOT calibrated or validated for any single site, and not for Warora/Vidarbha (no cold events there).
Station training series contain breaks (e.g. Hisar ~2010); labels are an imperfect reference.

Training RH is derived from GSOD mean temperature and mean dew point; Repo B measures RH directly. Daily aggregates (tmin, tmax, tmean, mean RH, lags, rolling stats) must be computed exactly as in src/features.py (build_feature_set + add_daily_range_features).
Decision threshold was tuned on validation seasons using the train-only model; the shipped model is refit on all seasons and has no held-out evaluation of its own.

Alert threshold (predicted next-day Tmin) sits well above the 4 C label because regression pulls cold-tail predictions upward; at this operating point roughly 3 of 4 alerts are false alarms (precision ~0.24).
No station-identity features are used, by design (the v1 Europe model failed this).
